question: Why is BCC so important in programs like malaria control?

options.A: People must be persuaded to consistently sleep under insecticide-treated nets
options.B: BCC automatically kills adult mosquitoes living near stagnant water pools
options.C: Insects understand health messages broadcasted over local radio stations
options.D: Communication programs replace the need for antimalarial drug treatments

explanation: You got it! Having mosquito nets in a box doesn't help if people refuse to hang and sleep under them every night.

question: What key details should a nurse document after speaking with a returning defaulter?

options.A: A list of grocery items the client purchased that morning
options.B: The exact cost of transport the client paid to reach the town
options.C: The personal opinions of the nurse regarding the client's family
options.D: The reason for missing appointments and the new plan agreed upon

explanation: Good records capture why they missed visits and the agreed care plan, ensuring smooth continuity of care no matter who is on duty next.

question: Which electrolyte level should you watch closely when giving a loop diuretic like furosemide?

options.A: Hypomagnesemia
options.B: Hypokalemia
options.C: Hypernatremia
options.D: Hypercalcemia

explanation: You've got this! Loop diuretics make the kidneys flush out extra water, sodium, and potassium, which can lead to low blood potassium (hypokalemia).

question: A mum who is exclusively breastfeeding her 2-month-old baby asks about natural birth control. What is required for the Lactational Amenorrhea Method (LAM) to work?

options.A: She must have experienced at least two normal menstrual cycles
options.B: She must practice exclusive breastfeeding and remain without menses
options.C: She must pump breast milk at least four times every night
options.D: She must supplement feeds with formula every night

explanation: LAM is a wonderful natural method, but it relies strictly on exclusive breastfeeding, a baby under six months, and no returned period yet.

question: What is the purpose of an EMR audit trail?

options.A: To automatically record every time a user opens or views a patient chart
options.B: To measure how fast a patient recovers from surgery
options.C: To monitor how many steps a nurse walks during a 12-hour shift
options.D: To track how much money the hospital spends on computer maintenance

explanation: An audit trail leaves a digital footprint, tracking who looked at a patient's file and exactly when they opened it.

question: Why are menstrual cycles often irregular during the first year or two after a girl's first period?

options.A: The thyroid gland temporarily stops working during adolescence
options.B: The uterus is still too small to hold a normal volume of blood
options.C: The cycles are frequently anovulatory as the endocrine system matures
options.D: Girls consume too much dietary iron during their growth spurts

explanation: You're getting the hang of this! Because ovulation doesn't happen every single month right away, it takes time for the hormonal system to settle into a steady rhythm.

question: A nurse only checks clinic records to decide what health program to build. What is the biggest downside to this?

options.A: It is too expensive for hospital computers
options.B: It stops doctors from writing prescriptions
options.C: It takes too many years to gather basic stats
options.D: It misses vulnerable people who never make it to the clinic

explanation: You got it! Clinic records only show those who could reach the facility. You might completely miss sick people who are too far away or can't afford transport.

question: Why are helper T-cells considered the master coordinators of the immune system?

options.A: They physically swallow large bacteria and digest them inside stomach acid.
options.B: They create a hard physical barrier around damaged skin to stop bleeding.
options.C: They release chemical signals that activate both B-cells and other T-cells.
options.D: They turn into red blood cells when the body suffers from severe anemia.

explanation: Helper T-cells act like military commanders, sending chemical messages to rally both B-cells and other T-cells into action.

question: An elderly client with limited mobility spends most of the day lying in bed. What is the most important preventive action the caregiver should take?

options.A: Leave the client alone for long hours to promote independence
options.B: Keep the bedroom completely dark to encourage deep sleep
options.C: Reposition the client frequently to protect skin integrity
options.D: Restrict all fluid intake to prevent bathroom accidents

explanation: Regular turning and repositioning relieve pressure on bony areas, which is critical for preventing painful pressure ulcers in bedbound clients. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T4#GNS324_U5_T4_h5)

question: What is the primary definition of ambulation in healthcare?

options.A: The physical therapy exercise routine
options.B: The ability of a patient to walk
options.C: The safe transfer from bed to chair
options.D: The prevention of blood clots in legs

explanation: Ambulation simply means walking, whether done completely on one's own or with the help of a device or another person. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T8#GNS324_U3_T8_h1)

question: What actually happens during DOTS (Directly Observed Therapy) for a TB patient?

options.A: A health worker watches the patient swallow every dose
options.B: Blood tests are run daily to measure drug levels in the serum
options.C: The patient reports their pill intake via phone once a week
options.D: Family members check the pill bottles at the end of each month

explanation: Under DOTS, a healthcare worker physically watches the patient take their meds to ensure they finish the whole course without missing days.

question: Why do the liver and kidneys suffer damage from toxins more often than other organs?

options.A: They are located closest to the digestive tract where toxins enter
options.B: They have thick protective walls that trap circulating poisons inside them
options.C: They produce natural antibodies that chemically react with heavy metals
options.D: They process, filter, and concentrate large volumes of blood in the body

explanation: Since these are the body's main cleaning and filtering organs, they naturally handle the highest amounts of circulating toxins.

question: What particle size is generally needed for medication to reach the deep lower airways and alveoli?

options.A: Between 50 and 100 micrometers
options.B: Greater than 20 micrometers
options.C: Between 1 and 5 micrometers
options.D: Any visible dust particle size

explanation: Fine particles measuring 1 to 5 micrometers are small enough to bypass the upper airway and settle deep in the bronchioles and alveoli. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h2)

question: What is the classic description of the walking pattern often seen in late pregnancy?

options.A: A fast shuffling stride
options.B: An unsteady staggering gait
options.C: A stiff-legged military march
options.D: A wide-based waddling gait

explanation: Pregnant women naturally widen their stance and swing their hips slightly more to maintain balance over relaxed joints and a heavy abdomen. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h5)

question: Why do doctors frequently combine chemotherapy with radiation therapy when treating advanced cervical cancer?

options.A: Chemotherapy prevents all future infections in the urinary tract
options.B: Chemotherapy drugs make cancer cells more sensitive to radiation damage
options.C: Radiation destroys the chemotherapy drugs before they harm healthy tissue
options.D: Chemotherapy eliminates the need for surgical removal of lymph nodes

explanation: Great clinical insight! In this case, the chemotherapy drugs act as helpers (radiosensitizers) that make the cancer cells weaker and much more vulnerable to being destroyed by the radiation.

question: How does a large local reaction differ from a normal insect sting reaction?

options.A: It indicates that bacteria have entered the wound and caused pus
options.B: It involves swelling greater than ten centimeters that peaks after a couple of days
options.C: It always causes immediate closing of the airway and low blood pressure
options.D: It means the patient is having a systemic IgE-mediated allergic response

explanation: Correct! A large local reaction is just a bigger, exaggerated inflammatory response at the site—it looks scary and spreads past 10cm, but it is not a true whole-body allergy.

question: What is a common mistake school administrators make when it comes to health policies?

options.A: Allowing students to write their own safety rules
options.B: Consulting too many medical professionals before acting
options.C: Making policies that are far too simple to understand
options.D: Drafting policies but failing to actually enforce them

explanation: That's right. Writing a great policy on paper won't help if management doesn't follow through and monitor it daily!

question: How can you best support parents whose baby is in Gallows traction?

options.A: Tell them not to touch the child at all
options.B: Explain the setup and involve them in gentle, non-physical comforting
options.C: Ask them to leave the room until it's over
options.D: Teach them how to adjust the heavy weights

explanation: Parents feel helpless seeing their baby in traction. Teaching them how to talk, sing, and stroke the baby keeps that parent-child bond strong!

question: Why do important minerals like iron and calcium need active transport to cross the placenta?

options.A: They can only travel when the mother's heart rate is very high
options.B: They are too large to pass through any membrane without being broken down
options.C: They dissolve directly into the amniotic fluid instead of fetal blood
options.D: They are moved against a concentration gradient to ensure the fetus gets enough

explanation: Active transport means the placenta uses energy to pump these minerals in—even if the baby already has more of them than the mother does! Nature makes sure the baby gets what it needs. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T5#GNS121_U6_T5_h5)

question: Which health issues are most common among children in chronically vulnerable homes?

options.A: Sports injuries from gym workouts
options.B: Malnutrition, stunted growth, and infections
options.C: Rare genetic disorders found only in rich families
options.D: High blood pressure from eating too much fast food

explanation: Correct! Poverty and poor sanitation expose children to hunger, poor physical development, and frequent illnesses like malaria and diarrhea.

question: What is one of the most effective nursing actions to stop the spread of resistant bugs in a ward?

options.A: Replacing all hospital water pipes every year
options.B: Isolating all patients who take vitamins daily
options.C: Practicing strict hand hygiene and infection control
options.D: Prescribing broad-spectrum drugs for every fever

explanation: Simple yet powerful! Good hand hygiene is your absolute best defense against carrying resistant germs from one patient bed to another. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T92#GNS214_U1_T92_h6)

question: Why is teaching patients preventive self-care so crucial before they leave the hospital?

options.A: To replace the need for any follow-up appointments
options.B: To make the discharge process take longer than necessary
options.C: To reduce the risk of recurring disorders and long-term complications
options.D: To ensure the patient never takes prescription drugs again

explanation: You got it! Good discharge teaching empowers patients to watch for warning signs and maintain their health at home.

question: Calculate the flow rate: 1000 mL of normal saline over 8 hours using tubing with a drop factor of 15 gtt/mL.

options.A: 60 gtt/min
options.B: 31 gtt/min
options.C: 208 gtt/min
options.D: 125 gtt/min

explanation: Math time! Multiply total volume (1000) by drop factor (15) to get 15,000. Divide by total minutes (480 mins in 8 hours), which gives 31.25—round it down to 31 drops per minute. You've got this!

question: Your hospital ward gets flooded with sudden admissions, leaving you short-staffed. What is the best way to handle patient safety?

options.A: Cancel all routine documentation and vitals checks for the entire day
options.B: Refuse admission to all incoming patients until the next shift arrives
options.C: Increase out-of-pocket treatment prices to immediately lower patient demand
options.D: Adjust staff assignments and prioritize urgent clinical care needs

explanation: Brilliant clinical thinking! When hands are few, a good nurse reorganizes tasks, focusing heavily on those whose lives are most at risk.

question: Which lab result do you expect to see when a patient has acute endometritis?

options.A: High blood glucose level
options.B: Elevated white blood cell count
options.C: Decreased red blood cell count
options.D: Low platelet count

explanation: Since the body is fighting a bacterial invader, the bone marrow pumps out extra white blood cells, leading to a high white blood cell count on the lab report.

question: A patient with high blood pressure stops taking their antihypertensive drugs because they feel fine. What is the most likely outcome of this action?

options.A: The body permanently adjusts and cures the hypertension naturally
options.B: The liver will start producing its own natural blood pressure medicine
options.C: Blood pressure will stay normal as long as the patient eats well
options.D: The patient remains at high risk for silent organ damage and stroke

explanation: Hypertension is a chronic condition managed, not cured, by medications. Stopping treatment causes blood pressure to rise again, silently damaging vital organs like the heart and brain. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T2#GNS215_U4_T2_h2)

question: What is the main reason we tell postpartum mothers to drink plenty of fluids and eat high-fiber foods?

options.A: To stop painful uterine afterpains
options.B: To turn lochia serosa into lochia rubra
options.C: To shrink the size of the bladder
options.D: To prevent postpartum constipation

explanation: Straining after delivery can be very painful, especially with stitches or piles (hemorrhoids). Fluids and fiber keep things soft and easy!

question: Why does the body need to control hormone release very carefully?

options.A: To keep blood volume extremely high at all times
options.B: To replace lost nerve impulses during physical stress
options.C: To ensure the kidneys filter blood at a constant rate
options.D: To prevent chaos in the body and keep things stable

explanation: Too much or too little of a hormone can upset your body's balance (homeostasis). Careful control keeps everything running smoothly!

question: What is the main goal of doing a community risk assessment?

options.A: Punishing communities that fail to follow sanitation laws
options.B: Reducing the total number of practicing nurses in a state
options.C: Preventing illness and health outbreaks before they occur
options.D: Generating revenue for private commercial pharmacies

explanation: Prevention is our superpower in public health! Finding risks early helps us stop sickness before it even starts.

question: A patient with mild arthritis struggles to open childproof medicine caps, so they leave bottles wide open on the table. What is the best nursing advice?

options.A: Advise the patient to use a hammer to break the stubborn plastic caps.
options.B: Take all the medication away and manage it from the nursing office.
options.C: Recommend easy-open non-childproof caps if no young children visit.
options.D: Scold the patient for leaving dangerous chemicals out in the open.

explanation: Brilliant! Making medicine packaging accessible helps them stay compliant with their treatment without risking injury from stubborn caps.

question: Why does severe anemia pose such a big risk to a woman during childbirth?

options.A: It leaves her with very little reserve to tolerate normal blood loss during delivery
options.B: It prevents the placenta from attaching securely to the uterine wall
options.C: It stops the uterus from producing amniotic fluid during the first trimester
options.D: It automatically causes the baby to develop severe congenital heart disease

explanation: Anemic mothers have low red blood cell counts, meaning even a small amount of blood loss during delivery can quickly lead to shock. This is why antenatal iron supplements are so crucial!

question: How do emergency contraceptive pills work after unprotected sex?

options.A: By thickening the uterine wall to trap the fertilized egg inside
options.B: By delaying or preventing the release of an egg from the ovary
options.C: By permanently destroying all active sperm inside the fallopian tubes
options.D: By causing an immediate surgical termination of an implanted embryo

explanation: Emergency contraceptives act like a pause button on ovulation. They push back the release of the egg so the sperm simply die out waiting. Simple and effective!

question: How can a nurse best stop a child in an oxygen tent from getting chilled by moisture?

options.A: Frequently dry the child's skin and change damp linens
options.B: Turn off the humidifier completely during the night shift
options.C: Apply petroleum jelly over the child's entire body
options.D: Open the canopy wide for one hour every morning

explanation: Regularly swapping out damp clothes and blankets prevents the moisture from chilling the child's body.

question: Which chemical messenger does the sympathetic nervous system release to speed up the heart?

options.A: Insulin
options.B: Norepinephrine
options.C: Bicarbonate
options.D: Acetylcholine

explanation: When your body needs an energy boost or gets stressed, sympathetic nerves release norepinephrine to tell the heart to beat faster and stronger!

question: Which simple tip helps your body absorb oral albendazole much better?

options.A: Ingesting the medication with a fatty meal
options.B: Crushing the tablet and dissolving it in cold water
options.C: Avoiding all fluids for two hours after dosing
options.D: Taking the pill on an empty stomach with vinegar

explanation: That's correct! Taking albendazole with a bit of fat helps your body absorb it much more effectively.

question: How is Type II FGM different from Type I?

options.A: It also includes removal of the labia minora
options.B: It leaves the clitoris completely untouched
options.C: It only involves stitching the vaginal opening shut
options.D: It is performed exclusively using modern surgical lasers

explanation: You nailed it! Type II goes a step further than Type I by also removing the inner labia (labia minora), and sometimes the outer labia too.

question: Why are older adults more likely to experience drug toxicity than younger adults?

options.A: Age-related decline in kidney and liver function
options.B: Older cells are completely immune to drugs
options.C: Their bodies absorb all medications instantly
options.D: They always take higher doses than prescribed

explanation: Spot on! Because the kidneys and liver process and clear drugs more slowly as we age, medications stay active longer, increasing the risk of buildup.

question: What is the main job of the plastic sheet found in a standard birth kit?

options.A: To provide a clean, moisture-barrier surface that prevents contact with floor pathogens
options.B: To wrap the newborn baby tightly to prevent sudden infant hypothermia
options.C: To cover the mother's abdomen during sterile abdominal examinations
options.D: To collect blood samples easily for laboratory testing after the delivery

explanation: Delivery floors and unsterilized beds carry lots of germs. The plastic sheet acts as a trusty barrier to keep things clean and safe for mama.

question: You feel the uterus and it is soft and boggy right after delivery. What is your very first action?

options.A: Apply warm compresses to the lower back
options.B: Administer oral pain relief medication
options.C: Transfer the patient to a tertiary hospital immediately
options.D: Perform immediate fundal uterine massage

explanation: Massage helps the uterine muscles tighten up and clamp down on bleeding vessels. It's a quick, lifesaving first step!

question: A nurse uses a dietary assessment to establish a baseline. What does this mean for patient care?

options.A: It provides a starting point to measure future nutritional changes and treatment progress
options.B: It acts as a permanent record that cannot be altered during the hospital stay
options.C: It proves that the patient has no underlying metabolic diseases
options.D: It serves as the final clearance for the patient to be discharged home

explanation: Establishing a baseline gives healthcare providers a reference point to see if interventions are helping or if the patient's condition is worsening. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T002#GNS227_U5_T002_h2)

question: What actually happens when there is 'sampling bias' in research?

options.A: An error caused by using a broken weighing scale in the clinic
options.B: The refusal of patients to answer personal questions in a survey
options.C: A systematic flaw that favors certain individuals over others in selection
options.D: The natural mathematical difference between a sample and a population

explanation: Spot on! Sampling bias means your selection method accidentally gives some people a better chance of being picked than others, skewing your results.

question: What is the difference between substandard and counterfeit medications?

options.A: Substandard drugs are manufactured locally, while counterfeit drugs are always imported.
options.B: Counterfeit drugs are cheaper versions of safe generics produced by licensed companies.
options.C: Substandard drugs fail quality specifications, while counterfeit drugs are deliberately mislabeled copies.
options.D: Substandard drugs have expired dates, while counterfeit drugs contain too much active ingredient.

explanation: Substandard drugs are usually genuine products that missed quality marks, while counterfeits are fake, fraudulent copies made to deceive us.

question: What shows that your discharge teaching for a stroke caregiver was truly effective?

options.A: Handing the family a large textbook on neurology on the day of discharge
options.B: Telling the family to call emergency services for any routine question
options.C: Assuming family members already know how to operate transfer belts
options.D: Teaching care techniques in small, manageable steps with return demonstrations

explanation: Having them show you back (return demonstration) is the best way to make sure they feel confident and safe doing it at home.

question: What is the very first action a nurse must take if a patient shows signs of a blood transfusion reaction?

options.A: Call the patient's family members
options.B: Stop the transfusion immediately
options.C: Administer prescribed antihistamines
options.D: Slow down the infusion pump rate

explanation: Stopping the infusion cuts off any further entry of incompatible or reactive blood products into the patient's circulation. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T8#GNS123_U2_T8_h7)

question: Why must a nurse avoid shaking clean or dirty bed sheets in a hospital ward?

options.A: It causes the cotton fibers to tear and stretch
options.B: It creates static electricity that damages monitors
options.C: It violates facility laundry sorting protocols
options.D: It spreads dust and germs into the surrounding air

explanation: You got it! Shaking sheets sends dust, skin flakes, and bacteria flying into the air, where they can settle on other patients or clean surfaces. Always fold or roll them gently instead!

question: A nurse notices feelings of personal discomfort when caring for a transgender patient. What is the most professional initial step to take?

options.A: Gently advise the patient to alter their outward gender expression
options.B: Ask another nurse to take over the assignment without explanation
options.C: Reflect on personal biases to ensure they do not affect the quality of care
options.D: Ignore the discomfort and assume it will go away on its own

explanation: Self-reflection is vital for nurses to manage personal attitudes so they can deliver objective, compassionate care to every patient regardless of background. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T1#GNS312_U4_T1_h8)

question: A community health nurse notices that pregnant women in her area always arrive late with severe complications. What is the best proactive step to take?

options.A: Wait until the government builds a new tertiary hospital nearby
options.B: Report the patients to local traditional rulers for punishment
options.C: Refuse to treat patients who arrive after their expected due date
options.D: Conduct community education on pregnancy danger signs and early clinic attendance

explanation: Proactive education is key! Teaching women about danger signs before complications arise helps them recognize trouble early and come to the clinic on time.

question: Why do upper urinary tract infections need pills or injections instead of simple vaginal creams?

options.A: Systemic drugs travel through the bloodstream to reach deep renal tissues effectively
options.B: Upper urinary tract infections are always caused by bacteria rather than yeast
options.C: Oral medications have zero side effects compared to localized vaginal creams
options.D: Topical creams are completely washed away by normal urinary output instantly

explanation: Creams only treat the surface down below. For deep infections up in the kidneys, the drug has to travel through the bloodstream.

question: What is the main goal of community-based rehabilitation programs in developing regions?

options.A: To eliminate the need for trained nurses and therapists
options.B: To replace all acute hospital medical care with home remedies
options.C: To bring rehabilitation services closer to local homes and families
options.D: To isolate disabled individuals inside specialized urban centers

explanation: Community-based care bridges the gap by bringing help directly to people in their local neighborhoods where specialized hospitals might be far away.

question: Why is inventory control considered a vital duty for ward nurses?

options.A: It prevents unexpected shortages of critical medical supplies during emergencies
options.B: It ensures that doctors write legible and accurate prescriptions daily
options.C: It completely eliminates the need for hospital management to buy new drugs
options.D: it stops patients from buying fake medications from outside pharmacies

explanation: Nurses manage ward stock so that life-saving items are always available when a patient suddenly deteriorates. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h1)

question: What exactly are intrinsic sugars?

options.A: Sugars naturally bound inside the cell walls of whole foods
options.B: Chemical preservatives used to extend shelf life in drinks
options.C: Refined sweeteners added to foods during factory processing
options.D: Artificial sweeteners that contain zero calories

explanation: You can think of intrinsic sugars as the good guys! They are safely locked inside whole, unprocessed foods like fruits and vegetables, right alongside healthy fiber.

question: What is a common barrier to maternal healthcare access driven by traditional gender norms in Nigeria?

options.A: Universal laws prohibiting women from entering clinics
options.B: A complete absence of medical facilities nationwide
options.C: Delayed spousal approval for healthcare finances
options.D: Biological immunity to pregnancy-related complications

explanation: Well reasoned! When men hold sole financial control, women sometimes have to wait for permission or money to get emergency obstetric care, which can be dangerous.

question: Why does a cut or break in the skin raise a patient's risk of getting sick?

options.A: Harmful germs can slip straight into the body without any barrier.
options.B: Langerhans cells stop working during healing.
options.C: Skin oil production increases so much that it traps bacteria.
options.D: The skin stops sweating, causing internal organs to overheat.

explanation: Great job! A whole skin barrier blocks germs effortlessly; once that barrier breaks, microbes have an open doorway into deeper tissues. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T3#GNS211_U2_T3_h7)

question: Why is a large-bore tube used for gastric lavage instead of a standard small feeding tube?

options.A: To make it easier for the nurse to push fluid deep into the small intestines
options.B: To ensure the fluid goes directly into the respiratory airway for safety
options.C: To allow pill fragments and food pieces to pass out without blocking the tube
options.D: To prevent the patient from experiencing any gag reflex during insertion

explanation: Small tubes easily clog with partially digested food or pill debris, rendering the wash ineffective; large-bore tubes provide a clear channel for thick debris to escape. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T12#GNS212_U1_T12_h3)

question: What is a windshield survey in community nursing?

options.A: Surveying doctors about vehicle preferences
options.B: Testing the vision of drivers in local transport parks
options.C: Observing a neighborhood by walking or driving through it
options.D: Reviewing hospital financial statements in an office

explanation: A windshield survey is a quick observational method where the nurse assesses community housing, sanitation, and general environment firsthand. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h4)

question: When caring for patients managing injections at home, what is a key duty for the nurse?

options.A: Disposing of patient sharps in regular household garbage bags
options.B: Instructing relatives to reuse syringes if they look clean
options.C: Teaching patients and families safe administration and disposal methods
options.D: Leaving used needles uncapped on the kitchen table for easy access

explanation: Great job! Educating patients and their families prevents accidental needle pricks in homes and communities after they leave the hospital.

question: A clinic spends its limited budget on new vaccines instead of fixing a leaking roof. What is the opportunity cost here?

options.A: The total financial value of the newly purchased vaccines
options.B: The electricity used to power the vaccine storage refrigerator
options.C: The salary paid to the clinic manager for making the choice
options.D: The protection and comfort lost from delaying the roof repair

explanation: Since they chose vaccines, the opportunity cost is the benefit they missed out on by leaving the roof unfixed for now.

question: Which patients are usually best suited for progestin-only pills instead of combined pills?

options.A: Patients with a high risk of bacterial skin infections
options.B: Individuals who require permanent surgical sterilization
options.C: Patients suffering from acute iron-deficiency anemia
options.D: Breastfeeding mothers who need to avoid estrogen

explanation: Estrogen can mess with breast milk supply and boost clotting risks. That's why progestin-only options are the go-to safe choice for breastfeeding mums!

question: Routine iron supplements are given during pregnancy mainly to prevent which condition?

options.A: Pregnancy-induced hypertension
options.B: Iron-deficiency anemia
options.C: Excessive amniotic fluid
options.D: Gestational diabetes mellitus

explanation: You got it! Since blood volume shoots up during pregnancy, extra iron helps make enough hemoglobin to stop anemia.

question: Why do adolescent girls need more iron in their diet?

options.A: To increase their overall body fat percentage
options.B: To prevent the onset of juvenile diabetes
options.C: To support rapid thickening of tooth enamel
options.D: To replace iron lost during monthly menstruation

explanation: Teens growing up face new changes; adolescent girls need extra iron to make up for what is lost during monthly periods and keep anaemia away.

question: What does a testable hypothesis need to have?

options.A: Approval from hospital administrators
options.B: Complex mathematical equations and proofs
options.C: Absolute proof that an intervention works
options.D: Variables that can be measured and observed

explanation: If you can't measure it in real life, you can't test it! A good hypothesis always uses observable things.

question: What is the main purpose of reviewing past adverse events and near misses in a hospital unit?

options.A: To find a specific staff member to blame for the mistake
options.B: To refine safety protocols and improve future patient care
options.C: To increase the cost of patient hospital bills
options.D: To reduce the number of shifts nurses have to work

explanation: Quality improvement treats mistakes and close calls as learning opportunities to fix broken systems rather than punish individuals. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T4#GNS321_U2_T4_h7)

question: What blood test results for reproductive hormones are typically seen in a woman going through menopause?

options.A: High FSH and low estrogen
options.B: High progesterone and low LH
options.C: Low FSH and high estrogen
options.D: Low progesterone and low FSH

explanation: When the ovaries slow down, estrogen drops. Without that brake pedal, the pituitary gland panics and pumps out massive amounts of FSH trying to get a response!

question: Which clinical sign helps you tell kwashiorkor apart from marasmus?

options.A: Bilateral pitting edema
options.B: Extreme loss of all body fat
options.C: High serum iron concentration
options.D: Rapid increase in bone length

explanation: Remember: Kwashiorkor is tied to severe protein lack, which leads to fluid retention (pitting edema), especially making the legs and face look swollen.

question: Which group is considered especially vulnerable in community health?

options.A: Wealthy urban property owners
options.B: Children under five years old
options.C: Employed corporate executives
options.D: Licensed medical practitioners

explanation: Great job! Under-fives are easily affected by infections and poor nutrition, making them a key focus for public health nurses.

question: Which method involves a nurse driving or walking through an area to observe living conditions firsthand?

options.A: Random clinical trial
options.B: Windshield survey
options.C: Laboratory blood screening
options.D: Surgical audit

explanation: Well done! Think of a windshield survey like taking a mental snapshot through a car window—you are out there observing housing, roads, and everyday life.

question: Which complication is a top cause of mothers dying during home deliveries?

options.A: Post-term pregnancy
options.B: Mild urinary frequency
options.C: Gestational diabetes
options.D: Postpartum hemorrhage

explanation: Heavy bleeding after birth happens fast and can be very dangerous—it's the leading killer of mothers in home birth settings.

question: How does an occupational therapist mostly differ from a physiotherapist?

options.A: Occupational therapists focus on adapting practical daily life tasks and home environments
options.B: Occupational therapists only work in intensive care units
options.C: Occupational therapists are licensed to prescribe medications
options.D: Occupational therapists deal exclusively with mental health disorders

explanation: While physiotherapists focus on body movement and strength, occupational therapists help patients master everyday chores like cooking, washing, and dressing.

question: What is a major giveaway that a digital blood pressure cuff has an air leak?

options.A: The screen flashes bright red and rings a loud alarm
options.B: The battery icon shows full charge the whole time
options.C: The machine shows an error code or cannot finish pumping up
options.D: The device measures the blood pressure twice as fast as usual

explanation: If air is escaping, the machine can't build up the pressure it needs, so it will usually flash an error message at you.

question: When trying to keep people safe from chemicals at work, what is considered the absolute best first step?

options.A: Conducting weekly medical tests on every worker
options.B: Handing out expensive protective gear to all staff
options.C: Putting warning signs on every single office door
options.D: Replacing a toxic chemical with a safer alternative

explanation: Brilliant! Substituting a dangerous chemical with a safer one completely removes the hazard instead of just managing the risk. Elimination is always the gold standard in safety.

question: What is another common name for infectious conjunctivitis?

options.A: Lazy eye
options.B: Crossed eyes
options.C: Night blindness
options.D: Pink eye

explanation: Conjunctivitis is widely called pink eye because the small blood vessels in the conjunctiva become swollen and irritated, giving the eye a pink or red appearance. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T3#GNS311_U3_T3_h3)

question: Why are routine screenings, like annual tuberculosis tests, so important for hospital staff?

options.A: They completely prevent bacteria from entering the hospital building
options.B: They catch potential occupational infections early before symptoms worsen
options.C: They replace the need for wearing masks during patient care
options.D: They test the patient population for chronic illnesses

explanation: Routine checks help catch any sneaky occupational exposures early on, meaning you can get treated quickly and stay healthy!

question: Why are schools considered great spots for public health interventions?

options.A: Schools have unlimited financial resources to buy medical equipment
options.B: Teachers possess advanced clinical degrees in nursing and medicine
options.C: Students are legally required to receive medical treatment at school
options.D: Children spend a large portion of their formative years gathered in one place

explanation: Spot on! When children are gathered in one learning spot, public health workers can easily reach many of them at once to build healthy habits.

question: Why should nurses avoid using heavy medical jargon when speaking with community patients?

options.A: Medical terms are forbidden in primary health care clinics
options.B: Using simple words takes too much time during consultations
options.C: It shows that the nurse lacks proper professional training
options.D: Patients may misunderstand their diagnosis and fail to follow treatment

explanation: Using everyday language ensures the patient truly grasps what is wrong and what they need to do to get better. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T12#GNS124_U5_T12_h3)

question: A researcher measures both blood pressure and salt intake among market traders on the same day. What type of study feature is this?

options.A: Testing a new blood pressure medication over time
options.B: Measuring exposure and outcome at the same time
options.C: Comparing historical records from ten years ago
options.D: Following patients after a surgical intervention

explanation: Spot on! Gathering info on both the suspected cause (salt) and the health outcome (blood pressure) simultaneously is the hallmark of cross-sectional work.

question: How does buying fruits in their natural season help families on a tight budget?

options.A: Farmers give away all seasonal fruits for free to hospitals
options.B: Seasonal fruits never require washing or preparation
options.C: Abundant supply during peak season drives market prices down
options.D: Government laws make out-of-season fruits illegal to sell

explanation: You got it! When farmers harvest a lot of a fruit during its peak season, the market price drops, making healthy eating budget-friendly.

question: What is the main goal of doing routine data validation at your clinic?

options.A: Replacing paper registers with permanent digital tablets instantly
options.B: Catching and correcting recording errors before report submission
options.C: Speeding up the physical delivery of drugs from international donors
options.D: Increasing the financial grants given directly to individual nurses

explanation: Spot on! Validation is just our safety net to catch small mistakes early so our reports go up the chain clean and correct.

question: What is the specific name for Cushing's syndrome when it is caused by a tiny tumor in the pituitary gland making too much ACTH?

options.A: Cushing's disease
options.B: Conn's syndrome
options.C: Pheochromocytoma
options.D: Addison's disease

explanation: Here is a handy clinical tip: 'Cushing's syndrome' is any excess cortisol, but when the pituitary gland's tumor is the culprit, we specifically call it 'Cushing's disease'.

question: Why are the standard 'rights' of medication administration so important if a legal case of negligence arises?

options.A: They are federal tax requirements for pharmaceutical companies.
options.B: They serve as the accepted standard of care to prove or disprove negligence.
options.C: They guarantee that hospitals will never face patient lawsuits.
options.D: They allow doctors to bypass writing paper prescriptions.

explanation: Exactly! The medication rights represent everyday nursing best practices. Courts look at them to see if standard care was followed.

question: What is the main job of white blood cells when an infection enters the body?

options.A: To defend the body by neutralizing foreign invaders
options.B: To transport oxygen to body tissues
options.C: To digest food and absorb nutrients
options.D: To regulate blood pressure and fluid balance

explanation: Your white blood cells are your body's frontline military defenders, always on patrol to hunt down and destroy invading germs.

question: What is the main job of foetal circulation?

options.A: To supply oxygen and nutrients from the mother
options.B: To pump blood directly into the mother's kidneys
options.C: To circulate air through the baby's developing lungs
options.D: To filter all waste through the baby's own kidneys

explanation: You've got this! Since a baby in the womb cannot breathe air or eat food yet, the placenta steps in to bring oxygen and nutrients straight from the mother's blood. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h1)

question: What does the first delay in the Three Delays Model refer to?

options.A: The time spent waiting for an ambulance on a bad road
options.B: The delay caused by nurses refusing to treat a patient
options.C: The time it takes for labor contractions to start
options.D: The delay in deciding to seek medical help

explanation: The first delay happens at the household or community level when family members fail to recognize danger signs or hesitate to seek care. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T44#GNS214_U1_T44_h3)

question: What special proteins does the body make to neutralize foreign invaders or antigens?

options.A: Enzymes
options.B: Antibodies
options.C: Platelets
options.D: Hormones

explanation: Spot on! Antibodies are the body's custom-built defense proteins that lock onto and disarm specific foreign invaders.

question: Why must instrument box locks and ratchets be kept open during the sterilization process?

options.A: To make it easier to count them after the cycle
options.B: To allow steam to reach all hidden surfaces
options.C: To make the instrument tray look neat and tidy
options.D: To prevent the metal handles from melting

explanation: Keeping hinges and box locks open ensures that the sterilizing steam makes full contact with every part of the metal. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h8)

question: Which mineral deficiency is particularly common in mountainous regions and areas far from the sea?

options.A: Calcium
options.B: Sodium
options.C: Vitamin C
options.D: Iodine

explanation: Iodine is naturally abundant in oceans and coastal soils, leaving inland and high-altitude regions vulnerable to low dietary intake. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T022#GNS227_U2_T022_h3)

question: What is the definitive treatment when acute foetal distress does not respond to conservative resuscitation?

options.A: Strict bed rest for the mother
options.B: Administration of oral antibiotics
options.C: Monitoring for another two hours
options.D: Emergency delivery of the foetus

explanation: If the baby remains starved of oxygen despite nursing interventions, the only way to save it is to deliver the baby promptly. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T003#GNS226_U4_T003_h6)

question: Which of these is a known risk factor for developing severe menstrual cramps?

options.A: Living in a warm tropical climate
options.B: Starting menstrual periods at a very early age
options.C: Having a short duration of menstrual bleeding
options.D: Starting menstruation after age sixteen years

explanation: Correct! Early menarche (getting your period before age 11) is linked to a higher chance of primary dysmenorrhoea.

question: What usually happens to stretch marks over time after delivery?

options.A: They fade from reddish-purple to silvery-white lines
options.B: They develop painful open ulcers that require suturing
options.C: They turn dark brown and raise above the skin surface
options.D: They completely disappear without leaving any trace

explanation: Stretch marks start out bright and angry-looking, but over time they calm down and fade into soft, silvery lines.

question: In community health, what does the term 'social stratification' mean?

options.A: The official administrative mapping done by the local government
options.B: The physical division of land into residential and industrial zones
options.C: The seasonal migration of farmers during the dry harvest period
options.D: The ranking of people into layers based on wealth, status, or power

explanation: Social stratification just means how society is layered into different groups based on wealth, influence, and social standing. Knowing this helps nurses spot who might be missing out on care.

question: What is the very first thing you must do if you suspect your patient is having a transfusion reaction?

options.A: Administer emergency antihistamines
options.B: Collect a urine sample for testing
options.C: Stop the blood transfusion immediately
options.D: Notify the attending physician

explanation: Safety first! Stop the infusion right away to keep any more of that mismatched blood from entering their system. Every second counts.

question: A pregnant woman at 28 weeks asks what her baby is mostly doing during this third trimester. What is the best way to answer?

options.A: Gaining weight, storing body fat, and maturing the lungs
options.B: Completing the process of implantation into the uterine lining
options.C: Forming the neural tube and starting the very first heartbeat
options.D: Creating all the major internal organs from basic germ layers

explanation: Well done! The third trimester is all about putting on healthy weight, growing bigger, and getting those lungs and brain ready for life outside the womb.

question: A nurse wants to find out the percentage of pregnant women at a clinic who sleep less than five hours a night. Which design fits best?

options.A: Experimental design
options.B: Randomized controlled trial
options.C: Ex post facto design
options.D: Descriptive design

explanation: Brilliant! When you are just counting or checking the frequency of a habit or symptom in a group without testing a new drug or treatment, you are doing a descriptive study.

question: Who is famous for introducing the 'total pain' concept in palliative care?

options.A: Cicely Saunders
options.B: Elisabeth Kubler-Ross
options.C: Florence Nightingale
options.D: Virginia Henderson

explanation: Spot on! Dame Cicely Saunders pioneered modern hospice care and taught us that pain is more than just physical—it includes emotional, social, and spiritual parts too.

question: What usually happens when health professionals bypass community input and decide problems alone?

options.A: Government funding increases because the staff showed independence
options.B: The community completes all health projects much faster
options.C: They often target issues that do not match the real priorities of the residents
options.D: Local disease rates drop instantly due to professional expertise

explanation: Without local consultation, healthcare workers may focus on problems that matter to textbooks rather than the community. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T17#GNS225_U2_T17_h5)

question: What is the best way to help a patient stick to their long-term blood pressure medication plan?

options.A: Telling the patient to stop taking pills whenever their blood pressure normalizes
options.B: Explaining that the medication controls the condition rather than curing it
options.C: Insisting that family members administer every daily dose orally
options.D: Warning the patient that stopping pills causes instant cardiac arrest

explanation: Fantastic! Patients often stop taking meds when they feel fine. Teaching them that the drugs are keeping their pressure under control helps them stay consistent for life.

question: Dizygotic (fraternal) twins are formed when:

options.A: Two separate eggs are fertilized by two separate sperm
options.B: A single fertilized egg splits into two parts
options.C: An unfertilized egg divides spontaneously
options.D: One egg is fertilized simultaneously by two different sperm

explanation: That's correct! Fraternal twins happen when the ovaries release two eggs, and both get fertilized independently. Think of them as brothers and sisters born at the exact same time!

question: Why does a subcutaneous injection take longer to work than an IV injection?

options.A: Injected drugs must travel through the liver first
options.B: Skin layers create a physical barrier to fluid movement
options.C: Subcutaneous fat actively destroys active drug molecules
options.D: Subcutaneous tissue has a limited blood supply

explanation: Think of it this way: fatty tissue has fewer blood vessels compared to veins, so it takes a little longer for the medicine to hitch a ride into your bloodstream!

question: Which qualitative approach specifically focuses on exploring the lived experience of a concept?

options.A: Ethnography
options.B: Phenomenology
options.C: Clinical trial
options.D: Grounded theory

explanation: You can remember this easily: Phenomenology looks at 'phenomena' or lived experiences to uncover what a specific human experience truly feels like.

question: Why are very young mothers at such high risk of developing obstetric fistulas?

options.A: Their pelvic bones are not fully developed, causing prolonged obstructed labor
options.B: They consume a diet that lacks adequate protein during pregnancy
options.C: Hormonal imbalances cause spontaneous weakening of the bladder wall
options.D: Traditional birth attendants intentionally damage the bladder during delivery

explanation: You nailed it. A young, narrow pelvis can trap the baby's head, pressing it so hard against the bladder and rectum that it cuts off blood flow and forms a fistula.

question: Why do nurses usually keep the head of the bed slightly elevated for a patient with high brain pressure?

options.A: To allow clearer visibility during frequent neurological checks
options.B: To help blood drain away from the head and lower pressure
options.C: To make it easier for the patient to swallow saliva safely
options.D: To prevent the lungs from collapsing during mechanical ventilation

explanation: Gravity is our friend here! Elevating the head helps blood flow smoothly out of the brain, keeping intracranial pressure down.

question: A clinic administrator is buying medications following the National Drug Policy. What should guide this choice?

options.A: Purchasing large quantities of single-use antibiotics regardless of disease patterns
options.B: Focusing on safety, efficacy, affordability, and availability of essential medicines
options.C: Stocking only medications that are heavily advertised on television and radio
options.D: Buying the most expensive imported brands to guarantee maximum patient prestige

explanation: When stocking a clinic, we always look for drugs that are safe, work well, patients can afford, and are actually available when needed!

question: Which of the following is an example of a three-dimensional instructional aid?

options.A: An audio podcast
options.B: A chalkboard drawing
options.C: A printed textbook page
options.D: Anatomical manikin

explanation: Three-dimensional aids have length, breadth, and thickness, allowing students to touch and examine physical structures like manikins and models. [learn more](GST321_U8_T4#GST321_U8_T4_h3)

question: What is the primary function of the cerebellum?

options.A: Regulating basic breathing and heart rate
options.B: Processing conscious thought and reasoning
options.C: Producing cerebrospinal fluid
options.D: Coordinating balance and smooth body movements

explanation: The cerebellum fine-tunes motor activity and helps maintain posture and balance during movement. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T1#GNS222_U3_T1_h2)

question: What main feature defines a traditional community in public health?

options.A: Having the exact same annual income level
options.B: Working in the exact same commercial sector
options.C: Being registered at the same local hospital
options.D: A shared geographic boundary and common interests

explanation: Think of a community as people living closely together in a specific area who share common values and daily lives. You've got this!

question: What is the main goal of a Drug Revolving Fund (DRF) in a hospital?

options.A: To ensure a steady and uninterrupted supply of essential medicines
options.B: To provide free medical treatments to all vulnerable populations
options.C: To pay the monthly salaries of clinical and administrative staff
options.D: To generate excess profit for hospital infrastructure development

explanation: Spot on! The DRF is like a rolling fund. Money from drug sales goes right back into buying more drugs so the pharmacy never runs empty.

question: What is the main clinical reason for using the Z-track method during an IM injection?

options.A: To speed up the systemic absorption rate of local anesthetics
options.B: To prevent irritating medication from leaking into subcutaneous tissue
options.C: To eliminate the need for skin antisepsis before the procedure
options.D: To reduce the overall depth required for deep muscle penetration

explanation: Z-track is a smart trick! By pulling the skin sideways before sticking, you create a zigzag path that locks harsh or staining medicines deep in the muscle where they belong.

question: According to Rubin's maternal role theory, what is the first major task an expectant mother focuses on?

options.A: Ensuring safe passage for herself and her child
options.B: Rejection of her own childhood parenting style
options.C: Immediate financial planning for college
options.D: Complete isolation from social networks

explanation: Spot on. Keeping herself and the baby safe and healthy is always the number one early priority for an expectant mum.

question: A patient is admitted with sudden, severe confusion and mood swings. What must the nurse consider first based on biological etiology?

options.A: Whether an underlying physical illness or hormone imbalance is causing the symptoms
options.B: How long the patient has been using herbal sleeping mixtures
options.C: Which family member caused the patient to feel stressed recently
options.D: If the patient experienced a difficult childhood in the village

explanation: Medical issues like thyroid problems or infections can cause psychiatric symptoms, so biological causes must be investigated during assessment. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T4#GNS314_U2_T4_h2)

question: What is the medical term for shortness of breath that happens specifically when a patient lies flat?

options.A: Apnea
options.B: Tachypnea
options.C: Orthopnea
options.D: Dyspnea

explanation: Orthopnea is a classic sign of heart failure where fluid shifts in the lungs when lying down, making breathing difficult. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T2#GNS213_U1_T2_h2)

question: Why is teaching patients how to use home blood pressure monitors such an important nursing duty?

options.A: Patients need to know how to solder broken circuit boards at home
options.B: Good technique prevents false readings that could lead to wrong medication changes
options.C: It stops patients from ever coming back to the hospital clinic
options.D: Home machines are so complicated that only rocket scientists can run them

explanation: If a patient uses poor posture or a bad cuff size at home, their doctor might see bad data and change their prescriptions incorrectly. Your teaching makes a real difference!

question: An experienced nurse is bored with routine duties and wants to take on hospital quality projects. What management approach fits best?

options.A: Reducing the nurse's daily patient assignment size
options.B: Focusing strictly on increasing the base hourly salary
options.C: Threatening disciplinary action for minor paperwork delays
options.D: Providing opportunities for professional achievement and growth

explanation: You nailed it! When a nurse is looking for a challenge, giving them room to grow and achieve is the best way to keep them inspired.

question: What is polypharmacy generally defined as?

options.A: Stopping all medications abruptly without advice
options.B: Taking five or more medications concurrently
options.C: Injecting a single drug twice a day
options.D: Using only traditional herbs for chronic illnesses

explanation: Polypharmacy refers to the use of multiple drugs at the same time, commonly set at a threshold of five or more. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T7#GNS215_U1_T7_h3)

question: Why is educating parents about their child's chronic condition so important?

options.A: It prevents the child from ever growing up
options.B: It turns parents into licensed medical doctors
options.C: It empowers them to provide safe daily care and advocate for their child
options.D: It ensures the parents never need to visit a clinic again

explanation: Well-informed parents can manage home routines effectively and speak up for their child's needs in healthcare settings. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a permissible reason for a nurse to breach patient confidentiality in routine clinical settings?

options.A: Specific legal mandates or court orders requiring disclosure for public safety
options.B: Assisted partner notification conducted with the client's explicit consent and safety clearance
options.C: Immediate threat of severe harm where professional intervention is legally required
options.D: Curiosity from extended family members who want to know why the patient is visiting the clinic

explanation: Family curiosity is never a valid reason to breach confidentiality; privacy rights protect patients from unauthorized snooping. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T8#GNS216_U6_T8_h8)

question: What is the standard bedside scale nurses use to quickly check a trauma patient's level of consciousness?

options.A: Braden Scale
options.B: Pain Numeric Rating
options.C: Apgar Score
options.D: Glasgow Coma Scale

explanation: You nailed it! The Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) checks eye, verbal, and motor responses so we can quickly tell how alert or responsive a patient is.

question: Why do inactivated (killed) vaccines usually need multiple doses or booster shots?

options.A: Inactivated vaccines dissolve in the bloodstream before reaching lymph nodes
options.B: The chemical preservatives used to kill the virus degrade the main antigen quickly
options.C: Killed pathogens cannot multiply in the body, so they trigger a weaker immune response
options.D: White blood cells cannot recognize dead pathogens without a live helper virus

explanation: Because the germ is dead, it cannot multiply to give the immune system a long workout. Boosters help remind the body to keep those defenses high!

question: A patient undergoing chemotherapy has a platelet count of 45,000/mcL. Which instruction is best?

options.A: Increase intake of green leafy vegetables to boost iron and clotting factors
options.B: Take high-dose aspirin daily to help thin the blood and improve circulation
options.C: Perform vigorous deep-tissue stretching exercises twice a day to prevent stiffness
options.D: Use an electric shaver instead of a traditional razor for daily grooming

explanation: Brilliant! Low platelets mean a higher risk of bleeding, so switching from sharp razors to electric shavers helps keep the patient safe from cuts.

question: What is the primary role of the subthalamus?

options.A: Processing the sense of smell and taste
options.B: Regulating the production of red blood cells
options.C: Producing hormones to control blood pressure
options.D: Coordinating smooth skeletal muscle movements

explanation: Spot on! The subthalamus teams up with the basal ganglia to make sure your body movements are smooth and controlled.

question: A public health team monitors school absenteeism and pharmacy sales of cough syrup during a flu season. What type of surveillance is this?

options.A: Passive surveillance
options.B: Laboratory surveillance
options.C: Syndromic surveillance
options.D: Sentinel surveillance

explanation: Syndromic surveillance tracks symptom clusters and related data before a formal lab diagnosis is confirmed. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T3#GNS313_U4_T3_h2)

question: What is the main reason the blastocyst hatches out of its protective shell (the zona pellucida)?

options.A: To allow the blastocoele fluid to drain out into the fallopian tube
options.B: To trigger the sudden production of human chorionic gonadotropin
options.C: To allow the trophoblast cells to physically attach to the uterine wall
options.D: To force the inner cell mass to divide into twin embryos

explanation: You got it! The zona pellucida acts like a temporary hard shell. Shedding it allows the sticky outer cells to finally attach to the womb.

question: What is the primary male surgical sterilization procedure called?

options.A: Tubal ligation
options.B: Vasectomy
options.C: Orchiectomy
options.D: Prostatectomy

explanation: A vasectomy blocks or cuts the vas deferens tubes to prevent sperm from entering the semen. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T1#GNS225_U3_T1_h4)

question: Which of these actions is a big no-no for a nurse working in the public civil service?

options.A: Attending mandatory nursing professional update workshops
options.B: Requesting standard medical history data from a patient
options.C: Consulting senior colleagues regarding complex patient cases
options.D: Diverting public hospital drugs for personal commercial sale

explanation: Using government supplies or hospital drugs for your own personal business is a serious violation of civil service ethics.

question: How does a vision statement differ from a mission statement?

options.A: A vision statement is created by junior staff, while a mission is written by the government
options.B: A vision statement looks forward to future aspirations, while a mission focuses on present purpose
options.C: A vision statement is kept secret from patients, while a mission is printed on posters
options.D: A vision statement deals strictly with daily nursing chores, while a mission covers finances

explanation: Visions describe a future desired state, whereas missions focus on what the organization is doing today. [learn more](GST321_U2_T3#GST321_U2_T3_h2)

question: Which of these is a high-alert medication that needs extra safety checks before you give it?

options.A: Standard saline eye drops
options.B: Intravenous heparin
options.C: Topical menthol ointment
options.D: Oral multivitamin tablets

explanation: Blood thinners like heparin are high-alert drugs. A small calculation mistake can cause serious bleeding, so double-check everything!

question: What is the most common cause of salpingitis?

options.A: Sexually transmitted bacteria
options.B: Autoimmune joint disorders
options.C: Fungal overgrowth from antibiotics
options.D: Congenital structural defects

explanation: Infections like Chlamydia and Gonorrhea are the main culprits behind most fallopian tube infections.

question: Why shouldn't patients chew or swallow sublingual or buccal medications right away?

options.A: The medication will instantly crystallize in the stomach
options.B: Swallowing destroys the first-pass effect protection and digestive enzymes may break down the drug
options.C: Swallowing increases the absorption speed too much
options.D: Chewing causes severe irritation to the inner cheek lining

explanation: If they swallow it like a regular pill, stomach acid and the liver (first-pass metabolism) will chew it up and weaken the drug before it even gets to work. Let it dissolve where it is!

question: Which action by a nurse violates a client's right to voluntary family planning?

options.A: Explaining how barrier methods prevent sexually transmitted infections
options.B: Asking the client about their future plans for having children
options.C: Strongly pressuring a client to accept a method the nurse prefers
options.D: Providing pamphlets written in the local language of the client

explanation: Coercion and pushing personal preferences onto clients violate the core ethical principle of patient autonomy and voluntary choice. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h4)

question: In a patriarchal family setup, who typically makes the final financial and health decisions?

options.A: The youngest child in the family
options.B: The maternal grandmother alone
options.C: The male head of the household
options.D: The local community traditionalist

explanation: In patriarchal settings, financial and key decision-making power usually rests with the male head. You've got this!

question: A patient's fasting blood sugar result comes back at 115 mg/dL. How should the nurse interpret this finding?

options.A: It is completely normal and requires no further follow-up.
options.B: It indicates prediabetes or impaired fasting glucose.
options.C: It confirms that the patient has full-blown Type 1 diabetes.
options.D: It shows severe hypoglycemia requiring immediate sugar intake.

explanation: Values between 100 and 125 mg/dL fall into the prediabetes range, signaling a need for lifestyle changes. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T12#GNS221_U2_T12_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT something you should do when managing a sudden laryngospasm?

options.A: Calling for immediate medical assistance and emergency help
options.B: Applying 100% oxygen via a face mask or bag-valve-mask
options.C: Administering a large volume of ice-cold water by mouth
options.D: Ensuring the patient's airway remains open and unobstructed

explanation: You nailed it! Never give water by mouth when someone is having an airway spasm or can't swallow properly—that's a major choking hazard.

question: How does successful disclosure directly support HIV treatment adherence?

options.A: It chemically alters the antiretroviral drugs to last longer in the bloodstream
options.B: It completely eliminates all possible side effects of the medication
options.C: Household members can offer practical reminders and emotional encouragement to take drugs
options.D: It forces the government to deliver medications directly to the patient's doorstep

explanation: Having a supportive person aware of the diagnosis helps patients take their daily medications consistently without hiding. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T8#GNS216_U6_T8_h4)

question: Why does severe peripheral vascular disease often lead to an amputation?

options.A: Blocked arteries prevent oxygen and nutrients from reaching tissues, causing cell death.
options.B: High blood pressure forces the limb to swell until the skin splits open.
options.C: Excess fluid builds up in the muscles and causes the bone to snap.
options.D: Weakened veins allow blood to pool and turn into dangerous blood clots.

explanation: Think of it like a plant without water—when blood flow is cut off, the tissue lacks oxygen and dies, which can create gangrene that requires surgery. Great job learning the basics!

question: What primary agent does an autoclave use to disinfect infectious medical waste?

options.A: Open flame combustion
options.B: High-pressure saturated steam
options.C: Concentrated liquid bleach
options.D: Ultraviolet sun rays

explanation: Autoclaves use intense, high-pressure steam to kill germs effectively without needing to burn the materials. A staple equipment in healthcare!

question: Which factor is most strongly tied to whether a woman uses modern contraception?

options.A: Age of the youngest grandparent
options.B: Employment in the banking sector
options.C: Level of formal education
options.D: Proximity to major airports

explanation: Studies consistently show that women with more formal education are better equipped to make informed choices and utilize modern family planning.

question: Which of the following measurement scales includes BOTH equal intervals and a true zero?

options.A: Ratio scale
options.B: Nominal scale
options.C: Interval scale
options.D: Ordinal scale

explanation: The ratio scale sits at the top of the ladder—it has both evenly spaced numbers and a real, absolute zero.

question: Which infection is most commonly spread when a healthcare worker accidentally suffers a needlestick injury?

options.A: Tuberculosis
options.B: Streptococcus
options.C: Hepatitis B
options.D: Malaria

explanation: Hepatitis B is very easily passed through blood and body fluids. That's why we are always extra careful with needles and sharps in clinicals!

question: Why is keeping our gut healthy so important for our overall wellbeing?

options.D: The gut produces red blood cells for circulation

question: What common complication happens when pieces of a heart valve growth break off and travel in the bloodstream?

options.A: Bone fracture

options.D: Asthma attack

question: What do we mean by the 'target population' in a research project?

options.C: The small group of nurses who help collect data at the clinic desk
options.D: The government officials who give permission to run the hospital study

explanation: Exactly! The target population is your ultimate group of interest—even if you can't physically reach every single one of them.

question: How many pairs of spinal nerves are in the human body?

options.A: 12 pairs

question: A patient recovering from a severe stroke struggles to walk and needs help rebuilding muscle strength. Which team member should be consulted?

options.A: Physician
options.B: Physiotherapist
options.C: Pharmacist
options.D: Social worker

explanation: You nailed it! Physiotherapists are experts at helping patients regain movement, strength, and independence after major setbacks like strokes.

question: Unexplained facial hair growth in a female patient can be a sign of which condition?

options.A: Chronic kidney disease
options.B: Polycystic ovary syndrome
options.C: Iron deficiency anemia
options.D: Essential hypertension

explanation: Correct! Extra facial hair (hirsutism) is often linked to higher androgen levels, which are common in polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS).

question: What is the term for a resting heart rate that drops below 60 beats per minute?

options.A: Tachypnea
options.B: Bradycardia
options.C: Hypotension
options.D: Tachycardia

question: What do we call the dangerous medical condition when core body temperature drops below 35°C?

options.A: Hypothermia
options.B: Vasodilation
options.C: Homeostasis
options.D: Hyperthermia

question: In some Nigerian households, men make most of the major decisions. How does this affect family planning?

options.A: Maternal mortality rates instantly drop to zero in rural regions.
options.B: Couples automatically adopt natural methods without needing education.
options.C: Health clinics stop stocking hormonal contraceptive injections.
