question: Why is it so nutritious to eat beans alongside maize or rice?

options.A: It achieves protein complementation by supplying all essential amino acids
options.B: It doubles the carbohydrate content without adding protein
options.C: It speeds up digestion so the stomach empties faster
options.D: It removes all toxic elements from the beans

explanation: Plant foods often lack one or two building blocks, but combining them (like beans and rice) covers all the bases to make a complete protein!

question: Which health history complaint needs an urgent neurological check right away?

options.A: Occasional muscle cramps after heavy exercise
options.B: Sudden changes in speech and vision
options.C: Temporary skin dryness in cold weather
options.D: Mild fatigue after a full night of sleep

explanation: Sudden trouble talking or seeing are major warning signs for a stroke or another urgent brain emergency. Always stay alert for these!

question: Which of the following is NOT one of the paired paranasal sinuses?

options.A: Maxillary sinus
options.B: Frontal sinus
options.C: Temporal sinus
options.D: Sphenoid sinus

explanation: The temporal bone does not contain a paranasal sinus; the four paired sinuses are maxillary, frontal, sphenoid, and ethmoid. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T3#GNS211_U4_T3_h4)

question: Why do working nurses need continuous professional development (CPD) programs?

options.A: Nursing councils require staff to sit for weekly written exams
options.B: It is the only way to prevent nurses from resigning from the job
options.C: Hospital management needs a way to reduce staff salary budgets
options.D: Medical knowledge and clinical technology change over time

explanation: Medicine never stays still! CPD helps nurses stay updated with new life-saving techniques, equipment, and medical knowledge throughout their careers.

question: What bad thing can happen when an operating room has a harsh, strict, and intimidating atmosphere?

options.A: Management will cancel all safety meetings for good
options.B: Patients will magically stop getting wound infections
options.C: Junior staff may be too scared to speak up about safety mistakes
options.D: Surgeons will finish every single surgery twice as fast

explanation: When people are afraid of being shouted at or humiliated, they stay quiet about errors. Teamwork and patient safety require an environment where everyone can speak freely.

question: Why does a patient with acute gastroenteritis experience watery diarrhea?

options.A: Pathogens trigger excess fluid and electrolyte secretion into the gut
options.B: Kidneys dump excess water directly into the large intestine
options.C: The stomach completely stops all digestive enzyme production
options.D: The liver stops producing bile needed to bind stool together

explanation: Toxins and cellular damage force the intestinal lining to secrete large quantities of water and salts, overwhelming the bowel's ability to absorb them. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h2)

question: Why do lung problems often affect the rest of the body?

options.A: Lung infections spread directly to the brain within hours
options.B: Every organ relies heavily on a steady supply of oxygen from the lungs
options.C: Poor breathing causes the stomach to stop digesting food completely
options.D: The heart stops pumping blood when the lungs become inflamed

explanation: You got it! If the lungs aren't working well, oxygen delivery drops, and every single tissue in the body starts to suffer. Oxygen is food for our cells!

question: Which of these is NOT a negative consequence of child marriage for a young girl?

options.A: Severe psychological trauma and social isolation
options.B: Permanent immunity against sexually transmitted infections
options.C: High risk of early adolescent pregnancy complications
options.D: Abrupt termination of her formal education

explanation: Correct! Child marriage definitely does not grant immunity to infections; starting sexual activity early often raises that risk instead.

question: What is the primary function of the pulmonary circuit?

options.A: Delivering nutrients directly to skeletal muscles
options.B: Pumping systemic blood to the lower extremities
options.C: Carrying blood between the heart and the lungs
options.D: Removing waste products from the brain tissue

explanation: The pulmonary circuit specifically handles the transport of blood from the heart to the lungs to pick up oxygen and release carbon dioxide. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T5#GNS111_U2_T5_h1)

question: Why is the "return-demonstration" method so effective when teaching a patient to test their blood glucose?

options.A: It proves the patient has memorized all medical terminology
options.B: It saves time compared to traditional verbal explanations
options.C: It confirms the patient can perform the skill correctly and safely
options.D: It eliminates the need for any written instructions

explanation: That's right! Having the patient show you how they do it ensures they truly grasp the steps before managing things at home alone.

question: What essential details should you include in your nursing notes after an ear exam?

options.A: A detailed diagram of the patient's skull bones and cranial nerves
options.B: The appearance of the canal, eardrum color, landmark visibility, and any abnormal findings
options.C: The exact brand and serial number of the otoscope device used
options.D: Only the patient's reported hearing test scores from previous years

explanation: Good clinical notes always describe what you actually saw—like the color of the eardrum and whether landmarks were clear—so you can track the patient's healing.

question: Which of the following describes an independent double-check for high-risk medication calculations?

options.A: The doctor and patient calculate the pill count together at discharge
options.B: The pharmacist calculates the dose and the nurse administers it without review
options.C: One nurse calculates the dose twice on two different patient charts
options.D: Two nurses calculate the dose separately without discussing their numbers beforehand

explanation: Independent double-checks require two clinicians to work out the math separately to catch hidden errors before administration. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T23#GNS122_U1_T23_h9)

question: A pregnant teenager attends an antenatal clinic and exhibits signs she is at risk of being forced into early marriage. What is the most appropriate initial nursing action?

options.A: Ignore the situation because family matters are private
options.B: Call local police immediately while she is still in the exam room
options.C: Lecture her parents harshly in front of the other waiting patients
options.D: Provide a safe, confidential space to assess her safety and offer support

explanation: Creating a confidential environment allows the nurse to gauge immediate danger and connect the patient with protective services safely. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T18#GNS312_U1_T18_h6)

question: What is the main goal of safe motherhood programs?

options.A: To shorten the duration of pregnancy
options.B: To reduce maternal and neonatal deaths
options.C: To promote exclusive formula feeding
options.D: To completely eliminate normal labor pain

explanation: Spot on! Safe motherhood programs are all about keeping both mothers and newborns safe, healthy, and alive. You've got this!

question: What is a major sign of compartment syndrome that sets it apart from normal fracture pain?

options.A: Severe pain that is not relieved by prescribed opioid pain medication
options.B: Sharp pain that completely disappears after taking deep breaths
options.C: Mild aching pain that occurs only when the patient stands up
options.D: Gradual itching underneath the cast as the bone begins to heal

explanation: When strong pain meds don't touch the pain at all, think compartment syndrome! It means dangerous pressure is building up inside the muscle.

question: How does a demand pacemaker operate during a normal heart rhythm?

options.A: It pumps extra blood to compensate for the fast natural rhythm
options.B: It shuts down completely and must be manually restarted by a doctor
options.C: It continuously sends rapid shocks to speed up the normal heartbeat
options.D: It remains idle and only fires when the natural heart rate drops too low

explanation: Demand pacemakers monitor the heart's natural electrical signals and only step in when the rate falls below the programmed threshold. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h2)

question: In benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), which part of the prostate gland usually enlarges first?

options.A: Anterior fibromuscular stroma
options.B: Central zone
options.C: Transition zone
options.D: Peripheral zone

question: Why is it so important to involve the community at every single stage of a health program?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for baseline surveys
options.B: It allows the government to avoid paying health workers
options.C: It ensures interventions address real, locally felt needs
options.D: It speeds up the construction of primary health centers

explanation: Spot on! When locals help plan from day one, we make sure we are actually solving the problems they care about most, rather than guessing what they need.

question: Which of these actions is NOT a good recommendation for nurse-led STI prevention education?

question: Why is it so powerful to involve traditional and religious leaders in your public health campaigns?

options.A: They hold high community trust, which greatly boosts local participation
options.B: They possess advanced medical degrees to treat complex diseases
options.C: They provide direct financial funding from international donors
options.D: They legally mandate citizens to buy private health insurance

explanation: People listen to their traditional and religious leaders! When these leaders endorse your immunization or health drive, the whole community is much more likely to show up.

question: What makes a research recommendation truly useful for clinical practice?

options.B: It avoids mentioning nurses and focuses solely on hospital administrators
options.C: It is broad enough to apply to every single medical condition
options.D: It is realistic, specific, and based directly on study findings

explanation: Good recommendations must be practical and grounded in your data so nurses can actually apply them on the ward.

question: A mother brings her healthy 14-week-old infant to the primary health clinic. Which group of vaccines is due for this visit?

question: What is the medical term for inflammation of the fallopian tubes?

question: A nurse uses a stethoscope to listen to bowel sounds after surgery. Which method of acquiring knowledge is this?

question: What is an important preventive screening topic for women receiving long-term home health care?

options.A: Daily testing for adult growth hormone levels

question: How does the principle of harmony of objectives help a hospital ward?

options.D: It helps staff achieve personal goals while meeting hospital aims

question: How do nurses determine if a specific disease rate in a community is a serious problem?

question: What does the acronym BLS stand for in nursing and emergency care?

question: What is the main goal of analyzing data collected from a community?

question: What is the name of the dilated pouch just beneath the nipple where milk pools?

question: A teenage girl comes in with pelvic pain and urinary problems. She looks terrified and refuses a physical exam. What is your best first move?

question: Why is agoraphobia often closely tied to panic attacks?

options.A: Agoraphobia only occurs immediately after a heart attack

question: Why must nurses carefully check a patient's medical history before recommending hormonal contraceptives?

question: A nurse manager says, 'We must sterilize the surgical instruments every morning at 7 AM.' What kind of activity is this?

question: How does unit dispensing improve financial transparency for patients?

question: How do screen-readers and talking appliances primarily help a visually impaired patient?

question: Why is it helpful for a nurse to check how much menstrual pain affects a patient's daily routine?

question: A patient is going home soon but needs a hospital bed and oxygen set up at their house. Who usually arranges this?

question: On a standard nursing line graph, what does the horizontal line (X-axis) usually show?

question: What is mostly packed inside the grey matter of the spinal cord?

question: What does 'confabulation' mean when caring for a patient with Korsakoff syndrome?

question: Why do nurses check both central pulses and listen to the chest when confirming death?

question: A nursing student is teaching a patient how to track her fertile window. Which recommendation gives the most accurate tracking?

question: Why must a community diagnosis look at factors like housing and clean water?

question: Which disease outbreak is most feared in overcrowded camps with poor sanitation?

options.B: Osteoporosis

question: What is compulsory before a patient takes part in a nursing research study?

question: A student nurse checks a drug's mechanism and possible side effects before giving it to a patient. Which historical role of nursing does this action reflect?

question: Why do pure scare tactics usually fail in teenage drug education programs?

question: Where do water-soluble peptide hormones usually find their target cell receptors?

question: You just received a new delivery of canned milk for the clinic pantry. Where should you put the new cans?

question: Which of these is NOT a standard data source used to track national family planning indicators?

question: Why must a nurse check a female patient's surgical history before placing an IV in her arm?

question: What is the main heart and philosophy behind home health nursing?

question: How does a polyvalent nurse usually support the healthcare team?

question: Which test is most commonly used to check for structural causes of secondary dysmenorrhoea?

question: Why do doctors often combine surgery with radiation or chemotherapy?

question: Why do healthcare providers recommend breathable cotton underwear and loose clothing to prevent infections?

options.B: They stop normal hormonal fluctuations from occurring

question: Why do doctors send the tissue from a removed cervical polyp to the lab?

options.B: To determine the patient's blood type

question: What is caput succedaneum?

question: Why is obstructed labor more common among very young mothers?

question: What is the main job of progesterone during the female reproductive cycle?

options.C: Stimulating the growth of breast milk ducts at birth
options.D: Lowering female body temperature during menstruation

explanation: Progesterone prepares the uterus to welcome a fertilized egg and keeps that lining comfy and stable so a healthy pregnancy can start.

question: Why are frontline nurses so important when figuring out why care processes vary?

options.A: They are the only hospital employees trained in advanced statistics
options.B: They spend most of their shift working away from the patient bedside
options.C: They hold the legal authority to rewrite hospital accreditation rules
options.D: They experience the daily workflow bottlenecks and supply issues firsthand

explanation: Spot on! Since you are right there at the bedside every day, you know better than anyone why certain workflow hiccups happen.

question: Why is it important for nurses to figure out if a patient's worsening condition is from the disease or from medical care?

options.A: To prove that doctors are always responsible for clinical outcomes
options.B: To determine if the injury resulted from care management or the illness
options.C: To ensure the hospital avoids paying any financial compensation
options.D: To decide which patients need emergency psychological counseling

explanation: Exactly! We need to know if the problem came naturally from the illness or if something in our care caused it, so we can fix our processes and help the patient better.

question: What should you do as a nurse if your home care plan isn't giving the results you hoped for?

options.A: Continue the exact same steps without making changes
options.B: Discharge the client from home care immediately
options.C: Wait until the client is admitted to the hospital
options.D: Revise the care plan with the interdisciplinary team

explanation: Brilliant! Nursing care is dynamic. If something isn't working, we team up and adjust the plan to better help our client.

question: What is the main purpose of regulatory bodies like the Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria?

options.A: To manage the commercial business accounts of private hospitals
options.B: To protect the public by ensuring safe and competent nursing practice
options.C: To manufacture pharmaceutical drugs for local distribution
options.D: To decide which political party wins national health elections

explanation: Spot on! Professional councils exist primarily to keep the public safe by setting high educational and ethical standards for all practicing nurses. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h7)

question: What is a key post-procedure instruction for a patient who received intravenous contrast dye during an MRI?

options.A: Avoid eating solid foods for the rest of the day
options.B: Take a strong diuretic medication immediately
options.C: Remain on complete bed rest for the next 24 hours
options.D: Drink plenty of fluids to help flush the contrast out

explanation: Increasing fluid intake helps the kidneys clear the contrast agent safely from the body. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T12#GNS123_U2_T12_h6)

question: What is a key preventative measure community health nurses should teach families about preparing meat?

options.A: Freezing meat at normal refrigerator temperatures for one hour
options.B: Cooking pork and beef thoroughly until no pink meat remains
options.C: Soaking steaks in vinegar to kill internal parasites
options.D: Washing raw meat with cold salty water before storing it

explanation: Spot on! Proper heat is the best defense; cooking meat well destroys any hidden larval cysts so they cannot infect humans.

question: What is the main job of a medical bougie?

options.A: To deliver high-flow oxygen therapy
options.B: To monitor internal body temperature
options.C: To navigate or explore narrow passages
options.D: To permanently remove tissue masses

explanation: Think of a bougie as a flexible guide. It's a slender tool used mainly to safely guide instruments or explore tight, narrow areas in the body.

question: What is the danger of giving very high megadoses of a single vitamin to an HIV patient?

options.A: It stops all drug interactions
options.B: It can cause toxicity or worsen viral replication
options.C: It completely replaces the need for water
options.D: It will cure the infection instantly

explanation: Correct! Just because a vitamin is natural doesn't mean more is always better. Megadoses can actually harm the body or help the virus multiply.

question: Why is giving incorrect drug information a serious ethical and legal mistake for a nurse?

options.A: It prevents the pharmaceutical company from selling more medications
options.B: It takes too much time away from routine ward cleaning duties
options.C: It can directly harm the patient and violates the professional duty of care
options.D: It lowers the overall financial revenue of the hospital pharmacy

explanation: You got it! Our primary duty is to protect our patients from harm, which means we must always provide accurate drug guidance.

question: A patient goes home with a PICC line for long-term IV antibiotics. Why use a central line here?

options.A: It safely accommodates prolonged, concentrated intravenous drug therapy outside the hospital
options.B: It prevents the patient from moving their arm during physical therapy
options.C: It allows nurses to directly irrigate the bone marrow every few minutes
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for any subsequent blood tests

explanation: A PICC line lets patients receive weeks of strong IV antibiotics safely at home without constantly getting poked in their regular arm veins.

question: Which animal is the primary natural reservoir and transmitter of Lassa virus to humans?

options.A: Migratory birds
options.B: Multimammate rats
options.C: Freshwater fish
options.D: Domesticated dogs

explanation: The multimammate rat sheds the Lassa virus in its urine and droppings, which can contaminate human food and living areas. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h3)

question: Why do clinics keep a 'buffer stock' of essential drugs?

options.A: To fulfill mandatory export quotas for foreign hospitals
options.B: To hide expired medications away from visiting inspectors
options.C: To prevent running out of drugs during unexpected supply delays
options.D: To increase the financial cost of routine patient treatments

explanation: Exactly! Think of buffer stock as your safety net so the clinic never runs dry when shipments are delayed.

question: Your patient just had talc pleurodesis and is crying out in sharp pain. What is your very first nursing action?

options.A: Tell the patient that chest pain is completely abnormal
options.B: Encourage the patient to take shallow, rapid breaths
options.C: Immediately pull out the patient's chest tube
options.D: Administer the prescribed pain medication promptly

explanation: Compassionate care is key! Sclerosants cause heavy inflammation and pain. Giving prescribed pain relief quickly helps your patient relax and take deep breaths again.

question: What does the abbreviation 'bid' mean on a medication order?

options.A: As needed
options.B: Before meals
options.C: Twice a day
options.D: Three times a day

explanation: You've got this! 'Bid' comes from the Latin 'bis in die', which simply means twice daily. You'll see this all the time on drug charts!

question: Why is that long plateau phase so important for the heart?

options.A: It speeds up the heart rate during periods of heavy physical exercise
options.B: It prevents the heart muscle from ever experiencing fatigue
options.C: It allows the pacemaker cells to reset their baseline electrical charge
options.D: It gives the heart enough time to fully squeeze blood out of its chambers

explanation: The plateau keeps the contraction going just long enough to push blood completely out into your body instead of just a quick twitch.

question: If a patient is severely dehydrated with low blood pressure, which hormones will their body release to help?

options.A: Large amounts of filtered glucose
options.B: Aldosterone and antidiuretic hormone
options.C: Decreased amounts of all electrolytes
options.D: Atrial natriuretic peptide only

explanation: Correct! Both aldosterone and ADH team up to hold onto salt and water, boosting your blood volume and cutting down urine output when you're dry.

question: A patient on hormone therapy for prostate cancer reports hot flashes and fatigue. How should you understand these symptoms?

options.A: Evidence of severe bone marrow suppression caused by the treatment
options.B: Early indicators of metastatic cancer spreading to the brain
options.C: Signs of an acute allergic reaction to the oral medication
options.D: Expected side effects resulting from artificially lowered hormone levels

explanation: Spot on! Lowering hormones mimics natural changes like menopause or andropause, which often brings tiredness and hot flashes.

question: What is the main goal of prescribing a beta-blocker for someone with angina?

options.A: Dissolving blood clots inside the coronary arteries
options.B: Widening narrowed airways in the lung tissues
options.C: Immediate relief of a sudden acute heart attack
options.D: Long-term prevention of chest pain episodes

explanation: Beta-blockers are like the steady guardians taken every day to keep future chest pain away by calming down the heart's workload.

question: How do newborns primarily generate body heat when they are exposed to cold environments?

options.A: Rhythmic skeletal muscle shivering
options.B: Metabolizing brown adipose tissue
options.C: Sweating through specialized skin pores
options.D: Rapid increase in respiratory rate

explanation: Unlike adults, newborns cannot shiver well; instead, they burn special brown fat stores to create and maintain body heat. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T51#GNS214_U1_T51_h4)

question: Why do doctors shorten the fertility testing timeline to just 6 months for women who are 35 or older?

options.A: Increased insurance coverage for fertility testing
options.B: Faster spread of sexually transmitted infections
options.C: Higher rates of voluntary childlessness in this group
options.D: Age-related decline in egg quality and reserve

explanation: Spot on! Because egg quality and number naturally start dropping faster after age 35, checking things a bit earlier helps protect their chances of starting a family.

question: How do standard precautions mainly stop infections from spreading?

options.A: By destroying the infectious agent inside the human body
options.B: By completely eliminating the natural reservoir of pathogens
options.C: By increasing the natural immunity of the susceptible host
options.D: By blocking the mode of transmission and portal of entry

explanation: You got it! Think of gloves and masks as road blockers. They stop germs from traveling from the patient to you, breaking the chain of infection right in the middle.

question: Why do nurses need to know normal pelvic anatomy?

options.A: It speeds up the patient discharge process.
options.B: It eliminates all risks of surgical complications.
options.C: It helps spot unusual changes and structural issues early.
options.D: It replaces the need for diagnostic lab tests.

explanation: Spot on! Knowing what a healthy pelvis looks and feels like is your superpower for catching abnormal shifts, growths, or malformations early during assessments.

question: A patient with a new leg cast says their toes feel very numb and tingly. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Perform a complete neurovascular assessment and report findings
options.B: Massage the toes gently to restore normal local blood circulation
options.C: Elevate the leg above heart level and encourage deep breathing
options.D: Administer a prescribed oral sleeping pill to calm the patient

explanation: Numbness and tingling are red flags for trapped nerves or poor blood flow. Checking thoroughly and reporting right away keeps the patient safe.

question: A hospital organizes a workshop on infection control. What result best proves the training actually worked?

options.A: An increase in the number of positive comments written about the guest speaker
options.B: A higher attendance rate compared to the previous hospital seminar
options.C: A larger collection of printed handouts left behind on the empty chairs
options.D: A noticeable decrease in hospital-acquired wound infections over the next month

explanation: When infection rates drop, it proves the nurses didn't just listen—they went back to the ward and put those safety practices into action!

question: In many homes, unfair food sharing puts which group at the highest risk of poor nutrition?

options.A: Young children and pregnant or lactating women.
options.B: Older teenage boys who play sports.
options.C: Elderly grandparents who live independently.
options.D: Adult male wage earners who work outside the home.

explanation: You're right! Even though their bodies need extra nutrients for growth and health, these groups often end up with the smallest shares.

question: Which tool is best used during a participatory needs assessment?

options.A: Random guessing of local statistics by the nurse
options.B: Observing patients only inside the tertiary hospital
options.C: Focus group discussions with community members
options.D: Closed-door cabinet meetings in the capital city

explanation: Focus groups allow residents to openly discuss and share their actual lived health experiences and needs. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T5#GNS124_U4_T5_h5)

question: What makes fetal hemoglobin so special compared to an adult's hemoglobin?

options.A: It changes color faster in bright light.
options.B: It carries more white blood cells.
options.C: It is immune to carbon dioxide poisoning.
options.D: It holds onto oxygen much more tightly.

explanation: Brilliant! Fetal hemoglobin grabs oxygen extra tightly so it can successfully steal oxygen away from the mother's blood across the placenta.

question: When a baby's head is nicely tucked with the chin to the chest, what is the measurement of the suboccipito-bregmatic diameter?

options.D: 9.5 cm

explanation: When the baby tucks its chin right into its chest, it presents its smallest and best measurement for birth: 9.5 centimeters. Beautiful design by nature!

question: What does a 'just culture' mean for patient safety in a hospital?

options.A: A strict legal system where every single mistake results in immediate court prosecution
options.B: An administrative rule that hides medical errors from patients and their families
options.C: A policy that protects senior doctors from ever facing disciplinary action
options.D: A work environment where staff can report errors openly to fix system flaws without unfair punishment

explanation: In a just culture, nurses feel safe speaking up about mistakes without fear, helping the whole team learn and protect patients better.

question: Why do we use a positive pressure room for an immunocompromised patient?

options.A: To make it easier for nurses to administer intravenous fluids quickly
options.B: To keep the room temperature warm enough for a patient with a fever
options.C: To blow contaminated air away from the patient so outside particles cannot enter
options.D: To suck all germs out of the patient's bloodstream through the ventilation vents

explanation: Wonderful! Positive pressure pushes clean air outward, acting as an invisible shield to protect a vulnerable patient from outside dust and germs.

question: Why do newborn babies need a vitamin K injection right after birth?

options.A: Breast milk contains zero traces of fat-soluble vitamins
options.B: Their liver is too large to process normal dietary proteins
options.C: Their sterile gut cannot yet synthesize the vitamin for blood clotting
options.D: They lose all stored maternal clotting factors during delivery

explanation: A newborn's tummy is completely sterile at first, meaning they don't have the gut bacteria needed to make vitamin K yet. The shot protects them from bleeding until their gut matures.

question: What is a great strategy to keep a patient from feeling overwhelmed during a health teaching session?

options.A: Using dense clinical terminology to sound authoritative
options.B: Breaking down information into small, digestible pieces
options.C: Handing the patient a complete medical textbook to read
options.D: Speaking as quickly as possible to cover all topics before shift change

explanation: Chunking info into bite-sized pieces prevents brain overload. Patients learn best when we take it step by step!

question: During which stage of sleep do you experience vivid dreams and temporary muscle relaxation?

options.A: Stage 3 NREM sleep
options.B: Stage 1 NREM sleep
options.C: Stage 2 NREM sleep
options.D: REM sleep

explanation: REM (Rapid Eye Movement) sleep is when most dreaming happens. Your body temporarily relaxes your muscles so you don't act out your dreams!

question: As a nurse, why shouldn't you focus only on the physical symptoms of a blood disorder?

options.A: Hospital management policies require psychological notes for discharge
options.B: Physical symptoms are rarely relevant to the patient's actual recovery
options.C: Emotional distress and physical pain deeply affect overall quality of life
options.D: Blood disorders only impact the emotional state of the patient

explanation: Spot on! Holistic nursing means remembering that a patient's mind and body are connected. Healing involves caring for both.

question: Why is localized swelling and extra blood flow actually a good thing when you have an infection?

options.A: It prevents any fluid from entering the damaged tissue spaces
options.B: It stops all cellular activity so the body can rest completely
options.C: It lowers local body temperature to kill heat-sensitive viruses
options.D: It brings white blood cells quickly to the site to fight invaders

explanation: Swelling and extra blood flow aren't just uncomfortable; they are high-speed delivery routes rushing white blood cells straight to the battlefield to clear out germs.

question: When doing a quick physical check, which sign helps you spot possible anaemia?

options.A: Swelling of the lower legs
options.B: Pallor of the conjunctiva
options.C: Yellowing of the sclera
options.D: Redness of the palms

explanation: Easy and quick! Pulling down the lower eyelid lets you check the conjunctiva. If it looks pale instead of nice and pink, it's a quick clinical clue that the blood count might be low.

question: Why is community education just as important as passing laws to stop FGM?

options.A: It allows communities to vote on whether they want to follow federal laws
options.B: It addresses the root cultural beliefs and social norms that sustain the practice
options.C: It ensures that traditional cutters can find alternative paying jobs easily
options.D: It replaces the need for police officers and court systems entirely

explanation: Well done! Laws alone cannot change deeply held mindsets. Education helps communities willingly choose to leave the practice behind.

question: How does knowing basic biographical data like a patient's age and gender help during a bone and joint assessment?

options.A: It helps identify risk factors associated with specific demographic groups
options.B: It measures the exact strength of the patient's muscle fibers
options.C: It proves whether the patient has an active bacterial infection
options.D: It provides a definitive diagnosis without needing further tests

explanation: Exactly! Knowing age and gender helps you anticipate certain health conditions that are more common in specific groups.

question: Why are sequential compression devices (SCDs) often used for patients in skeletal traction?

options.A: To reduce swelling by pushing fluid into the weights
options.B: To prevent deep vein thrombosis from immobility
options.C: To stimulate muscle growth while the bone heals
options.D: To anchor the patient's leg so the rope stays taut

explanation: Spot on! Staying still slows down blood flow in the legs, putting patients at risk for blood clots (DVT). SCDs gently squeeze the legs to keep the blood moving nicely.

question: What is a major social challenge faced by a family that refuses to follow local traditions regarding early marriage?

options.A: Mandatory community service penalties
options.B: Automatic promotion to local leadership roles
options.C: Immediate deportation from the region
options.D: Community ostracization and social isolation

explanation: Spot on! Families who step away from deeply held local norms often face heavy pressure, rejection, and isolation from their neighbors.

question: What is a key benefit of presenting research at a scientific conference?

options.A: Guaranteeing automatic acceptance into international print magazines
options.B: Eliminating the need to ever write a formal research paper
options.C: Getting immediate feedback and networking with other professionals
options.D: Receiving a cash prize from the hospital management board

explanation: Conferences allow researchers to talk directly with peers, answer questions on the spot, and build useful professional relationships. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T2#GNS224_U4_T2_h3)

question: What is the main job of the Bartholin's glands?

options.A: To secrete mucus for lubrication
options.B: To produce the female egg cells
options.C: To maintain acidic vaginal pH
options.D: To filter waste from the blood

explanation: Correct! These glands release fluid to keep the vaginal opening lubricated.

question: How is Type 2 diabetes different from Type 1?

options.A: Type 1 can be cured entirely with proper diet and oral medication
options.B: Type 2 only affects elderly individuals who consume high amounts of sugar
options.C: Type 2 involves insulin resistance and relative deficiency rather than complete beta cell destruction
options.D: Type 1 is caused by lifestyle factors while Type 2 is strictly genetic

explanation: In Type 2, the body still makes insulin, but the cells just don't respond to it well (resistance), and the pancreas can't keep up with the extra demand. You're mastering the basics!

question: A hypertensive patient keeps missing clinic days and stopped taking their drugs. As their nurse, what is your best next step?

options.A: Assume the patient is completely cured and stop calling their phone number
options.B: Conduct a home visit to discuss barriers to compliance and provide tailored education
options.C: Discharge the patient permanently from the clinic registry without further discussion
options.D: Report the patient to local law enforcement authorities for policy violation

explanation: Wonderful nursing judgment! Visiting them helps you find out why they stopped—maybe money is tight or side effects are bothering them—so you can help find a solution together.
